questions.text: Why do students make poor health choices according to the text?
opts: Motivation, habit, and priority — not lack of knowledge
questions.correct: Motivation, habit, and priority — not lack of knowledge
questions.hint: "They know perfectly well... The issue is motivation, habit, and priority."

questions.text: How much sleep do adults need per night?
questions.hint: "Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep per night."

questions.text: What percentage of students experience significant anxiety or depression?
questions.hint: "Between 30 and 40 percent of university students experience clinically significant levels of anxiety or depression."

questions.text: The texts say social connections protect against severe mental health problems.
questions.hint: "Students who feel genuinely connected to at least one other person are significantly less likely to experience severe mental health difficulties."

questions.text: WKU's student counselling service is ___ — you don't have to be in crisis to use it.
questions.hint: "It is there. It is free. You don't have to be in crisis to use it."

questions.text: What does the text say anxiety commonly manifests as?
questions.hint: "Anxiety most commonly manifests as perfectionism, procrastination, and avoidance."

questions.text: What symptoms does Rustam describe at the doctor's?
questions.hint: "Feeling really tired... some headaches... finding it hard to concentrate in lectures."

questions.text: Why does the doctor say coffee is bad for hydration?
opts: Coffee is a diuretic — it dehydrates you
questions.correct: Coffee is a diuretic — it dehydrates you
questions.hint: "Coffee is a diuretic — it actually dehydrates you."

questions.text: The doctor says Rustam's symptoms are consistent with ___ and poor nutrition.
questions.hint: "Your symptoms are consistent with sleep deprivation and poor nutrition."

questions.text: What does the doctor say about vitamins?
opts: A multivitamin is fine but supplements don't replace a proper diet
Only take vitamins prescribed by a doctor
questions.correct: A multivitamin is fine but supplements don't replace a proper diet
questions.hint: "A general multivitamin wouldn't hurt. But you shouldn't rely on supplements — they don't replace a proper diet."

questions.text: What exercise does the doctor recommend for Rustam?
questions.hint: "You don't have to do intense training. Even a twenty-minute walk helps."

questions.text: What will happen if Rustam's symptoms don't improve in two weeks?
opts: He will come back for a blood test
He will be referred to a specialist
questions.correct: He will come back for a blood test
questions.hint: "If things don't improve in two weeks, come back and we'll do a blood test."

questions.text: "You should drink more water." — "Should" means:
questions.hint: "should" = advice; a recommendation. Not as strong as "must" or "have to". ✅

questions.text: "You shouldn't skip meals." — "Shouldn't" means:
opts: I advise against it — it's a bad idea
questions.correct: I advise against it — it's a bad idea
questions.hint: "shouldn't" = advice against doing something. ✅

questions.text: "You don't have to take vitamins." — This means:
opts: Taking vitamins is not necessary — optional
questions.correct: Taking vitamins is not necessary — optional
questions.hint: "don't have to" = not obligatory. Optional. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ submit the form by Friday." (he/she/it form of have to)
questions.hint: "she" → HAS TO. "She HAS TO submit." ✅

questions.text: "I ___ wait an hour at the clinic yesterday." (past obligation)
questions.hint: Past of "have to" = "HAD TO". "I HAD TO WAIT an hour." ✅ Never "musted"!

questions.text: "must not" vs "don't have to" — which means FORBIDDEN?
questions.hint: "must not" = FORBIDDEN. "don't have to" = not necessary (optional). ✅

questions.text: "You should have slept earlier." — This means:
opts: You didn't sleep early — that was a mistake
You are able to sleep earlier
questions.correct: You didn't sleep early — that was a mistake
questions.hint: "should have + pp" = past criticism. You didn't do it, and you should have. ✅

questions.text: "She shoulds exercise." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: Modal verbs NEVER add -s! ✅ "She SHOULD exercise." ✅

questions.text: "Sleep deprivation is common." "Deprivation" means:
questions.hint: "deprivation" = the state of not having enough of something essential (like sleep).

questions.text: "Exercise has an antidepressant effect." This means:
opts: Exercise is a type of medicine
questions.hint: "antidepressant" = fighting or reducing depression. Exercise has this effect.

questions.text: "Sleep is therapeutic." "Therapeutic" means:
opts: Having a healing or beneficial effect
questions.correct: Having a healing or beneficial effect
questions.hint: "therapeutic" = healing; having a positive effect on health.

questions.text: "Anxiety manifests as avoidance." "Avoidance" means:
questions.hint: "avoidance" = the act of keeping away from situations that cause anxiety.

questions.text: "PE was compulsory at school." "Compulsory" means:
questions.hint: "compulsory" = required; you have no choice.
